Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
30 September 2026 .
Brent $ 103.68 + 0.03 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 L'Orient Today reports three ships were attacked Tuesday in the Strait of Hormuz; gCaptain says three more tanker attacks have surfaced through delayed UKMTO reports.

02 Iran is reviewing the US ceasefire counterproposal, per The National Desk, WXLV and KBOI, with Strait of Hormuz terms still unclear.

03 Brent stood at $103.68, up 0.03%, as of 16:08 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic, with fresh attack reports compounding the throughput collapse. L'Orient Today reports three ships were attacked Tuesday in the strait; gCaptain reports that three additional tanker strikes have surfaced through delayed UK Maritime Trade Operations filings, and tradewindsnews.com reports several ships were attacked as Iran launched fresh strikes. The attacker has not been identified in any of those reports. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. The rial hit a record low, per Pluang. Brent was at $103.68, up 0.03%, as of 16:08 UTC. The site has indexed 58 events in the last 24 hours. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, rising over 24 hours, flagged low-confidence because two of its inputs are stale or missing (Manifold forward contracts and Kalshi forward contracts), with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
